sections.name: schema
sections.doc: The `.env.schema` language this repository is written in.

keys.name: version
keys.doc: `version = 1` names the `.env.schema` language version. penv reads every version from 1 up to its own; a newer one is an error that tells you to run `penv upgrade`.
keys.if_wrong: [schema] version takes a whole number, such as 1

keys.name: preload
keys.doc: `preload = false` stops `penv run` loading its masking into the Node, Bun, Deno and Python processes it starts, so only `penv run`'s own output is masked. It applies only when you run penv yourself in a terminal; under an AI agent or a pipe the preload stays on.
keys.if_wrong: [run] preload takes true or false; penv ignores this value and preloads

sections.name: local
sections.doc: How sensitive values are written to `.env` files on this machine.

keys.name: encrypt
keys.doc: `encrypt = true` makes `penv set`, `penv pull` and `random()` write sensitive values to `.env` files as `enc:v1:...`, keyed in this machine's keychain, instead of plain text. `penv encrypt` rewrites the files and switches it.
keys.if_wrong: [local] encrypt takes true or false; penv ignores this value and writes plain text

sections.name: public
sections.doc: Key prefixes that ship to the browser.

keys.name: prefixes
keys.doc: `prefixes = ["APP_PUBLIC_"]` treats `APP_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` as not sensitive, as penv already treats `NEXT_PUBLIC_` and `VITE_` keys, so its value is not masked. A key with that prefix marked `@sensitive` is an error.
keys.if_wrong: [public] prefixes takes a list of strings, such as ["APP_PUBLIC_"]; penv ignores what is not one

sections.name: url
sections.doc: URL parts shown in plain text though the URL is sensitive.

keys.name: public
keys.doc: `public = ["scheme", "host"]` lets `url($DATABASE_URL, host)` print the host in plain text, while the password and the rest of the URL stay masked. `password` is never public; `check` fails if you list it.
keys.if_wrong: [url] public must be a list of URL parts

sections.name: hash
sections.doc: Keys whose `hash()` result is shown in plain text.

keys.name: public
keys.doc: `public = ["API_KEY_FP"]` shows the fingerprint `API_KEY_FP=hash($API_KEY, algo=sha256, length=8)` computes in plain text, so you can tell which key a machine has; a key marked `@sensitive` stays masked. Each entry must be a key whose value is a `hash()` call, or `check` fails.
keys.if_wrong: [hash] public must be a list of keys

sections.name: json
sections.doc: One section per key whose `json()` reads may be shown in plain text: `[json.GCP_SA_JSON]`. The section must name a key `.env.schema` declares, or `check` fails.

keys.name: public
keys.doc: `public = ["client_email"]` under `[json.GCP_SA_JSON]` lets `json($GCP_SA_JSON, client_email)` print the email in plain text, while the private key and the rest of the document stay masked.
keys.if_wrong: public must be a list of read paths

sections.name: hosts
sections.doc: The hosts each key with a computed `@hosts` may reach. `penv check --pin-hosts` writes it; `check` fails and a sealed run refuses while the computed hosts differ from the pin.

entries.doc: `DATABASE_URL = ["db.internal.example"]` pins the hosts `DATABASE_URL` may reach. Run `penv check --pin-hosts` to write it after you change where the key points.
entries.if_wrong: a [hosts] entry takes a list of hosts; penv reads this one as pinning no hosts

sections.name: rotation
sections.doc: The day each key was last written on this repository's machines. `penv set` writes it; `@rotate` reminders count from it.

entries.doc: `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY = "2026-09-22"` is the day `penv set` last wrote `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`; `@rotate=90d` on that key counts its 90 days from here.
entries.if_wrong: a [rotation] entry takes a date in quotes, such as "2026-09-22"; penv ignores this one

sections.name: providers
sections.doc: Where a provider's API is, when it is not the default: `[providers.penv]`.

keys.name: url
keys.doc: `url = "https://penv.internal.example"` points penv at that API for this provider instead of its default. `PENV_URL` in the environment wins for the default provider.
keys.if_wrong: url takes a string, such as "https://penv.internal.example"; penv ignores this value and uses the default

sections.name: targets
sections.doc: Per-language settings for `penv gen`, written when you run it: `[targets.ts]`. A field here wins over the same field of the target's own `target.toml`.

keys.name: output
keys.doc: `output = "src/env.ts"` is the file `penv gen` writes for this target.
keys.if_wrong: output takes a path in quotes, such as "src/env.ts"

keys.name: options
keys.doc: `[targets.ts.options]` holds the target's options, such as `runtime = "vite"`. `penv gen` writes each with a comment that says what it does.
keys.if_wrong: options is a section, such as [targets.ts.options]
